references.text: The rest of the grain offering shall belong to Aaron and his sons. It is most holy, part of the Lord's food offerings - this indicates the priests' right to eat from the holy gifts.
Describes how Aaron and his sons are to eat what remains of the grain offering - it is most holy and must be eaten in a holy place.
All male priests may eat from the sin offering - it is most holy, corresponding with the right to eat from the most holy gifts.
All male priests may eat the guilt offering in a holy place - it is most holy and relates to the priests' right to holy gifts.
Detailed rules about who may eat from the holy gifts in the priest's household, clarifying the context of who has the right to eat what is holy.
The priests' share of the most holy offerings that are not burned - this confirms the priests' right to eat from both the most holy and the holy.
Ezekiel's vision of the future temple confirms that the priests shall eat grain offering, sin offering, and guilt offering - a continuation of the principle of the priests' right to holy gifts.
